description: The Reserve Bank of Australia publishes statistics on the volume and value of payments made through Australia's payment systems, covering debit, credit and charge cards, ATM withdrawals, cheques, direct entry transfers and the New Payments Platform, and the real-time gross settlement system that settles high-value payments between banks. It is produced by the Reserve Bank of Australia from returns by financial institutions and payment system operators. Coverage is national for Australia, mostly from 2002 with some series back to 1985, at monthly and quarterly frequency. Tables are downloadable free as XLSX files from the payments data page. Caveats: series have breaks when reporting rules or participants change, the page read does not state a reuse licence, and the data are national totals, not regional or per-operator flows. For simulation it gives baseline transaction volumes and values for modelling payment system capacity and how outages of card networks, ATMs or settlement systems would disrupt economic activity, and for resilience studies of financial infrastructure. It is related to the ECB TARGET2 liquidity stress test case study record in this catalogue, on settlement system stress, and to the RBA retail payments reliability disclosures record, which reports outages.
